title: DNA extraction from stool
author: Veronika Pettersen
materials: Samples were mechanically lysed using the FastPrep-24 5G instrument (MP Biomedicals, USA)and subsequently centrifuged at 10,000 × g for 1 minute. A volume of 200 µL of the resulting supernatant was transferred to a deep-well plate for DNA extraction. The extraction was performed using the Tecan Fluent liquid-handling platform (Tecan, Switzerland) according to the ZymoBIOMICS 96 MagBead DNAprotocol (Zymo Research). DNA was eluted in 50 µL of EB buffer (Qiagen, Germany) and stored at –20 °C .

steps.title: Thaw and homogenize stool samples
steps.instruction: Thaw fecal samples, add DNA Genotek liquefaction reagent, and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Add internal spike‑in control
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of Vibrio campbellii culture (10⁴ cells/µL) to each sample as an internal spike‑in.

steps.title: Transfer to bead‑beating tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer 800 µL of the mixture to ZR BashingBead lysis tubes containing a mixture of 0.1‑mm and 0.5‑mm beads.

steps.title: Include extraction batch controls
steps.instruction: Prepare a positive control (75 µL ZymoBIOMICS Microbial Community Standard + 725 µL liquefaction reagent) and a negative control (700 µL liquefaction reagent + 100 µL Vibrio campbellii culture, 10⁴ cells/µL) in each extraction batch.

steps.title: Extract DNA from stool
steps.instruction: Perform mechanical lysis in the bead‑beating tubes, then extract DNA using the GenFind V3 reagent kit with the Bacteria protocol (Beckman Coulter).

steps.title: Quantify DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with the QuantIT High Sensitivity dsDNA Assay on a Tecan Spark plate reader.

steps.title: Spike samples with Alicyclobacillus DNA
steps.instruction: If concentration > 1.1 ng/µL, add Alicyclobacillus acidophilus DNA at 1 % of total input; if ≤ 1.1 ng/µL, supplement with Alicyclobacillus DNA to reach 50 ng total per reaction. Also spike the negative sequencing control with Alicyclobacillus DNA.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing libraries
steps.instruction: Use 50 ng of input DNA and the MGI FS Library Prep Set to construct libraries.

steps.title: Assess library quality
steps.instruction: Evaluate library size distribution with an Agilent TapeStation D1000 kit and re‑measure concentration using the QuantIT assay.

steps.title: Pool and circularize libraries
steps.instruction: Pool libraries in equimolar amounts to a final concentration of 100 pM, circularize with the MGI Easy Circularization Kit.

steps.title: Sequence libraries on DNBSEQ‑T7
steps.instruction: Sequence the pooled libraries on the MGI DNBSEQ‑T7 platform using 150 bp paired‑end reads.

steps.title: Check raw read quality
steps.instruction: Run FastQC v0.11.9 on the paired‑end reads.

steps.title: Trim adapters and low‑quality bases
steps.instruction: Filter adapters and low‑quality reads with Trim Galore v0.6.10 using default parameters.

steps.title: Remove human contaminant reads
steps.instruction: Map reads to the human reference genome (GRCh38, downloaded 2022) with Bowtie2 v2.4.43 using --very-sensitive --end-to-end; retain unmapped pairs using SAMtools v1.12 with -f 12 -F 256.

steps.title: Taxonomic profiling with MetaPhlAn4
steps.instruction: Run MetaPhlAn4 v4.0.6 against the CHOCOphLAN database to obtain taxonomic profiles.

steps.title: Resistome mapping with Bowtie2
steps.instruction: Map reads to the CARD nucleotide_fasta_protein_homolog_model (v3.2.9) using Bowtie2 v2.4.4 with the –very-sensitive‑local parameter.

steps.title: Filter ARGs and calculate RPKM
steps.instruction: Using SAMtools v1.12, separate mapped/unmapped reads, sort and index; retain ARGs with ≥80 % coverage; compute reads per kilobase per million mapped reads (RPKM) for each ARG; exclude efflux‑pump and metabolic‑function genes.

steps.title: Quantify MGEs with ShortBRED
steps.instruction: Identify MGE marker families from MobileOG v1.6 using shortbred_identify.py with --clustid 0.95; quantify reads with shortbred_quantify.py and normalize to RPKM.

steps.title: Estimate replication rates with CoPTR
steps.instruction: Apply CoPTR v1.1.4 to calculate peak‑to‑trough ratios for E. coli and K. pneumoniae.

steps.title: Strain analysis with StrainGST
steps.instruction: Download 102 B. longum reference genomes (20 Oct 2025), build a StrainGE v1.3.3 database (available on Zenodo DOI:10.5281/zenodo.17671286), and run StrainGST to detect strains.

steps.title: Assemble metagenomes with MEGAHIT
steps.instruction: Assemble quality‑filtered reads into contigs using MEGAHIT v1.2.9 with default parameters.

steps.title: Assess assemblies with MetaQUAST
steps.instruction: Run MetaQUAST (part of QUAST v5.2.0) on assemblies using the -m 1000 option.

steps.title: Functional pathway profiling with HUMAnN3
steps.instruction: Run HUMAnN v3.0.1 on filtered reads to obtain community‑level and species‑resolved MetaCyc pathway abundances; merge per‑sample tables with humann_join_tables; renormalize to relative abundances with humann_renorm_table.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of pathways
steps.instruction: Test pathway abundance differences with Mann–Whitney U test and Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction; analyse unstratified and stratified outputs focusing on High and Low Bifidobacterium clusters.

steps.title: Culture stool for ESBL‑E detection
steps.instruction: Plate eSwab‑collected fecal samples on ChromID ESBL agar (BioMérieux) and non‑selective blood agar; incubate at 35 °C for 18–24 h; consider samples with no growth on blood agar invalid; report samples with no growth on ESBL agar as negative.

steps.title: Identify ESBL‑E colonies
steps.instruction: Identify suspect colonies to species level by MALDI‑TOF MS (Bruker Daltonik) and confirm ESBL phenotype with the double‑disk approximation test (Liofilchem).

steps.title: Select high‑quality isolate‑metagenome pairs
steps.instruction: From 250 metagenomic samples, retain 47 with cultured ESBL‑E isolates; remove low‑quality or unsequenced isolates (n=10) and samples with >1 isolate (n=7); keep the remaining 32 samples for host validation.

steps.title: Extract DNA from ESBL‑E isolates
steps.instruction: Extract isolate DNA using the GenFind V3 reagent kit with the Bacteria protocol.

steps.title: ONT sequencing of isolates
steps.instruction: Sequence isolates on an Oxford Nanopore GridION using R10.4.1 flow cells and the rapid SQK‑RBK114‑96 barcoding kit.

steps.title: Base‑call ONT reads
steps.instruction: Perform base‑calling with Dorado v7.6.7 using the super‑accurate model dna_r10.4.1_e8.2_400bps_sup@v4.3.0.

steps.title: Filter and assemble ONT reads
steps.instruction: Filter reads with fllong v0.2.1; assemble genomes with Autocycler v0.4.0; circularize all genomes.

steps.title: Assess isolate assemblies
steps.instruction: Evaluate assembly quality with fast_count and QUAST v5.2.0.

steps.title: Identify ARGs in isolates and metagenomes
steps.instruction: Run Abricate v1.0.1 with CARD v4.0.1 on both isolate and metagenome assemblies, applying 99 % sequence identity and length thresholds; assign ESBL genes using CARD_AMR_clustered.csv; determine species with Speciator v4.0.0.

steps.title: Predict ORFs on ARG‑containing contigs
steps.instruction: Select contigs >1000 bp that harbor Abricate‑identified ARGs; predict open reading frames with Prodigal v2.6.3 (default).

steps.title: Assign taxonomy to ORFs
steps.instruction: Compare predicted amino‑acid sequences to the NCBI non‑redundant database using DIAMOND v2.1.6 with -evalue 0.00001, -id 95, and -query‑cover 95; for contigs assigned to multiple species, retain only those where ≥75 % of ORFs map to a single species.
